# ADR 0023 — The hexagon's craft layer: one term, one name per role, keys translated by table

> **In short.** In the context of a hexagon whose boundaries ADR 0011 and ADR 0018 state, facing code that kept the
> boundaries but named, translated and configured things in its own way per file, we decided for one term for domain
> folders, one name per role, exceptions translated through typed tables, configuration parsed by a schema and one
> test convention, shown on one feature end to end, and against leaving the craft to each session, to make a file's
> place and name follow from its role, accepting a few more files at every edge.

## Context and problem

The boundaries are stated and checked: what may import what (ADR 0011, 0018) and the file pattern of the core
(ADR 0021). How a feature is built inside them is not. The branch's code showed the gap: one adapter file broke the
pattern and escaped the guard's port pairing, five adapter classes put the technology before the port, an adapter
threw plain `Error`s that reached the user as raw text, the command line mapped every exception key to one exit code,
the asset pipeline's configuration had no schema and fell back to the path `missing`, and "Command" meant a use
case's input in ADR 0011 and a command line entry point in the app. ADR 0011 says `domain/<Context>/`, ADR 0021 and
the core rule say `domain/<Aggregate>/`.

## Decision drivers

- A file's name and place follow from its role, so every session places it the same way.
- No outside failure reaches a user as raw text, and no edge forgets a key.
- A wrong configuration stops the start; it never runs on a default for something that must be given.
- Someone new reads one example and can build the next feature without another project.

## Considered options

- **A — One craft layer, decided once, shown on one feature end to end.**
- **B — The craft left to each session, corrected in review.**

## Decision

Chosen: **A**, sheets `pix57-clean-branch` and `pix57-plan-approval-v2` of 2026-10-12 (F2, F3), because B is how the
drift above arose.

1. **The domain folder is named for its aggregate.** `domain/<Aggregate>/` in PascalCase; a bounded context of ADR
   0011 point 10 is a modelling term and holds one or more aggregate folders. A value object is a schema in its
   aggregate folder, `<name>.schema.ts`, not a file in a folder of its own. `[Agent adversarial-review]`
2. **Every role has one name** (table below). Adapter files are `<port>-<technology>.adapter.ts` exporting
   `<Port><Technology>Adapter`; exception keys are `<aggregate>.<snake_key>`; a command line entry point is
   `src/cli/<verb><Noun>.handler.ts` exporting `<verb><Noun>Handler`; "Command" keeps its meaning as a use case's
   input. `[Hook architecture-guard · Agent adversarial-review]`
3. **An adapter turns every outside failure into a core exception with a key.** A failed process, a refused request
   or a missing file becomes the port's exception; a plain `Error` never leaves the infrastructure package. The lint
   sees the errors an adapter builds; the review sees those it would let pass from a Node call.
   `[Lint no-restricted-syntax throw Error · Agent adversarial-review]`
4. **Each edge translates keys through a typed table.** A `Record` from the exception key enum to the edge's answer
   (exit code and message, HTTP status, WebSocket error); a key without an answer does not compile.
   `[Gate verify-full: type check]`
5. **Configuration is parsed by a core schema at the app's start.** `domain/<Aggregate>/<name>Config.schema.ts`
   parses the environment in the app; a default exists only for a value that is not a secret, and a failed parse
   stops the start with the schema's message. `[Agent adversarial-review]`
6. **Tests follow the layer.** A spec lies beside its file as `<file>.spec.ts`. A use case is tested with a
   hand-written `InMemory<Port>` fake that implements the port; an adapter with fakes for the process, the file system
   or the network that it receives; an edge with one case per key of its table.
   `[Gate check-tests · Agent adversarial-review]`

| Role | File | Exported name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Domain type, schema, enum | `domain/<Aggregate>/<name>.interface.ts`, `.schema.ts`, `.enum.ts` | the type, schema or enum |
| Use case input | `application/service/<verb><Noun>Command.ts` | `<Verb><Noun>Command` |
| Use case | `application/service/<name>.service.ts` | `<Name>Service` |
| Exception | `application/exception/<aggregate>.exception.ts` | `<Aggregate>Exception` |
| Exception key | `application/exception/<aggregate>ExceptionKey.enum.ts` | members `PascalCase = '<aggregate>.<snake_key>'` |
| Port | `port/outgoing/<name>.interface.ts` | `I<Name>` |
| Adapter | `adapter/<Area>/<port>-<technology>.adapter.ts` | `<Port><Technology>Adapter` |
| Configuration | `domain/<Aggregate>/<name>Config.schema.ts` | `<name>ConfigSchema` |
| Command line entry point | `src/cli/<verb><Noun>.handler.ts` | `<verb><Noun>Handler` |
| Edge table | `src/cli/<aggregate>ExitCode.ts` | `<aggregate>ExitCode` |
| Fake | inside the spec | `InMemory<Port>` |

### Consequences

- Good, because a file's role is readable from its name, and the guard pairs ports with their adapters.
- Good, because a new exception key fails the type check at every edge that has not answered it yet.
- Bad, because every edge carries a table and every outside call a translation.
- Binding modules, request validation, persistence and transactions follow with the server stack's ADR.

### Confirmation

`scripts/probe-architecture.sh` plants an adapter file outside the pattern and turns the guard red;
`scripts/probe-lint.sh` plants a `throw new Error` in the infrastructure package and turns lint red. The render
feature below is the reference implementation: the spec of its exit code table answers every key with its own code,
and `pnpm typecheck` fails when a key is removed from the table.

## Mechanics

One feature end to end, rendering one image under the memory guard, in the order it is built. Every step names where
its file goes and why there.

| Step | File | Why there |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `packages/core/src/domain/Render/renderJob.schema.ts`, `renderResult.interface.ts`, `renderStatus.interface.ts`, `renderConfig.schema.ts` | Decides without touching the outside: domain. |
| 2 | `packages/core/src/application/exception/render.exception.ts`, `renderExceptionKey.enum.ts` (`render.busy`, `render.memory_pressure` and seven more) | The failures the use case can name. |
| 3 | `packages/core/src/port/outgoing/localRenderer.interface.ts`, `renderMachine.interface.ts` | What the use case and the start need from outside, in domain types. |
| 4 | `packages/core/src/application/service/renderImageCommand.ts`, `renderImage.service.ts` with its spec and an `InMemoryLocalRenderer` | The use case: its input as a command, parsed into a render job before the renderer starts. |
| 5 | `packages/infrastructure/src/adapter/Render/localRenderer-mflux.adapter.ts`, `renderMachine-local.adapter.ts`, each with its spec, beside the adapter's own parts `renderLock.ts`, `onDisk.ts`, `mfluxComplaint.ts`, `judgeMemory.ts`, `readMemory.ts`, `renderLogRow.ts`, `runEnd.enum.ts`, `memoryAction.enum.ts`, `memoryReading.interface.ts` | Touches processes and files: adapter; translates every failure into a key. |
| 6 | `apps/asset-pipeline/src/renderConfig.ts`, `src/cli/renderImage.handler.ts`, `src/cli/showRenderStatus.handler.ts`, `src/cli/renderExitCode.ts`, `src/cli/exitAnswer.ts`, `src/cli/pipelineCommand.enum.ts`, `src/runPipeline.ts` | Parses the configuration, wires the port to the adapter, translates keys. |
| 7 | `packages/protocol` | Only when the result crosses the wire; this one does not. |

## Rejected

- **B — the craft left to each session.** It produced the drift this ADR fixes.
- **Folders per kind inside a domain folder** (`enum/`, `constant/`, `service/`). Flat files with a type suffix
  already say the kind.
- **An HTTP status inside a core exception.** The core does not know its edges; the table at each edge does.
- **A shared default for a missing value.** It hid a missing path behind the word `missing` and ran on.
